  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",

This example estimates an age-standardized exposure-response curve from simulated
county mortality counts. Exposure is measured once per county-year, while counts and
population denominators are reported separately for three age groups. The simulation
suppresses counts between 1 and 9 to illustrate how to fit the model when the exact
outcome is unavailable. All counties, exposures, and counts below are simulated.

## Simulate county-year counts

```{r simulate}
library(discoverHTE)

set.seed(2026)
units <- expand.grid(county = seq_len(60), year = 1:3)
units$unit <- seq_len(nrow(units))
units$x <- rnorm(nrow(units))
units$exposure <- 10 + 0.6 * units$x + rnorm(nrow(units), sd = 1.5)

ages <- c("65-74", "75-84", "85+")
panel <- units[rep(seq_len(nrow(units)), each = length(ages)), ]
panel$age <- factor(rep(ages, nrow(units)), levels = ages)
panel$population <- sample(1200:3500, nrow(panel), replace = TRUE)
rate <- exp(-5.8 + 0.35 * (as.integer(panel$age) - 1) +
              0.05 * (panel$exposure - 10) + 0.12 * panel$x)
count <- rnbinom(nrow(panel), mu = panel$population * rate, size = 10)
suppressed <- count >= 1 & count <= 9
panel$deaths <- ifelse(suppressed, NA_integer_, count)
panel$lo <- ifelse(suppressed, 1L, count)
panel$hi <- ifelse(suppressed, 9L, count)
table(suppressed)
```

## Estimate the curve

Pass the age group, population denominator, county-year identifier, and censoring
bounds to `method_negbinomcens()`. Exact counts have identical lower and upper
bounds. Suppressed counts enter the model through their interval. The outcome model
uses the age-specific counts and offsets, and the exposure-response curve is estimated
at the county-year level. Supply the county identifier to `estimate_erf()` to account
for repeated observations within counties.

```{r fit}
fit <- estimate_erf(
  deaths ~ exposure | x, data = panel,
  method = method_negbinomcens(
    age = "age", population = "population", unit = "unit",
    censor_lo = "lo", censor_hi = "hi", k_exposure = 5L, k_conf = 5L
  ),
  cluster = ~county, bw = 1, n = 30L
)
fit$erf(c(9, 11))$est
```

The two estimates are age-standardized rates per 100,000 at simulated exposure
levels of 9 and 11. The [methods paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.30838)
describes the empirical study and its data sources. The study draws on mortality counts from [CDC WONDER](https://wonder.cdc.gov/),
particulate matter estimates from the [Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group](https://sites.wustl.edu/acag/datasets/),
and county covariates from the [American Community Survey](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs).
